items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the county law and the executive law, in relation to the
reporting of a veteran's suicide
items.lawCode: Amd §677, County L; amd §353, Exec L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6807

SPONSOR: HELMING
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the county law and the executive law,
in relation to the reporting of a veteran's suicide

 
PURPOSE:

This bill establishes another method to keep track of veterans' suicides
rates.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the County Law to add a new subdivision to direct a
coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner to report, through the
use of a one page form, to the Division of Veterans' Affairs, any death
which appears to be a suicide by a person who is believed to be a veter-
an.

Section 2 amends the Executive Law to add a new subdivision directing
the Division of Veterans' Affairs to develop a one page form to be used
by a coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner for reporting any
death which appears to be a suicide by a person who is believed to be a
veteran.

Section 3 establishes that the Division of Veterans' Affairs must estab-
lish and implement the procedures and forms necessary for implementation
of this act within 60 days.

Section 4 establishes an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

According to the Pentagon's annual suicide report, active duty military
suicides hit a record high in 2018, jumping by 13%.  Additionally,
according to the 2019 National Veteran Suicide Prevention Report, the
number of veteran suicides has exceeded 6,000 each year from 2008 to
2017.

In November 2017, the New York State Suicide Prevention Task Force was
created. This past April, the Task Force released a report on its find-
ings. Among its many findings specifically related to veterans, the Task
Force found that veteran suicide rates are significantly higher than
those rates of non-veterans.

One common theme found in both national and state reports is the issue
of the data. Current data is inaccurate and incomplete and to fix the
problem, we must understand the problem. This legislation is an attempt
to improve the suicide surveillance data methods to gather more informa-
tion on veterans' suicide rates. If a coroner or the person acting on
his/her behalf has reason to believe there has been a suicide by a
veteran, he/she shall notify the Division of Veterans' Affairs through
the use of a simple one page form.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately and directs the Division of Veterans' Affairs to establish
and implement the procedures and forms necessary for implementation
within 60 days.

summary: Provides that the coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner shall promptly report to the division of veterans' affairs, in a one page form developed and provided by such division of veterans' affairs, any death which appears to be a suicide by a person who, to the knowledge of the coroner, coroner's physician or medical examiner, is a veteran.
